To: Leadership Team
From: Supply Chain Director
Date: Today
Subject: Network shipping plan to meet all requirements at the lowest total cost

Situation
We operate a network of warehouses and factories that must supply multiple stores and customer locations. Each origin holds limited inventory, while each destination has a firm requirement and service expectations. Freight rates differ by lane, and shipments must be made in whole-unit quantities (no partial loads). Managing this balance effectively is essential to control transportation spend and protect on-time, in-full delivery performance.

Problem
We need a consolidated shipping plan that, for each origin–destination lane, specifies how many whole units to dispatch so that:
- No origin sends more than it has available.
- Every destination receives its full requirement.
- The overall mix of lanes results in the lowest possible total freight cost.

Approach and next steps
- Use the attached data on available units by source, required units by destination, and per-lane shipping costs to build a feasible, whole-unit shipping plan.
- Produce a lane-level allocation that meets every destination’s need without exceeding any origin’s availability, highlighting the resulting total transportation spend and any residual inventory.
- Share the recommended plan for approval; upon sign-off, align carriers and site teams for execution and monitor first-cycle performance to validate service and cost outcomes.
